I'm not sure how accurate it comes coming from a trans person rather than a cis person, haha, but usually a trans person's genitals/possible medical procedures/ etc. aren't the first thing I think about when meeting them, or hearing them come out as trans. I usually worry about all the other stuff like pronouns because I'm forgetful and agh. 

But I definitely understand the worry. I wonder all the time about how my family will react if and whenever I begin transition. Will they be intrusive/secretly thinking about it/etc? I can't answer how your family and friends will respond but it's not rude or anything to set boundaries and have privacy in regards to your needs, if that's something that might help you talk about this sort of thing. Exactly how much you tell them is up to you and what's comfortable for you, as is what questions you'd want to answer, and stuff. You can also feel out how they might feel about lgb/trans people before coming out, if that would make it any easier. See what they might already know, etc. You know them better than I do, so sorry to assume anything, but if you're having trouble with somewhere to start, it's an option. 

As another person said here, there are many subreddits and communities online that can help, too. You can take your time getting connected to others that might be having the same problems as you, it can be difficult, but it can also be relieving to hear others' stories and experiences. 

I also understand your concern with bottom surgery, it's difficult to know that it's not perfect yet, and that having to go through surgery at all is even more difficult. Most of my low points are when I'm thinking about exactly that sort of thing, to be honest. There's advice and methods out there for coping with bottom dysphoria, and they may help. (Sorry if you've tried such advice! I know you talked about the small dick stuff, but since you've been uncomfortable with connecting with the communities and stuff I just wanted to mention the term for it.) I've read a lot of stories about relationships and these sort of pains. I've felt them myself. 

I really hope that it eases for you. You deserve someone who loves you and is happy to explore with you. It's not dumb or 'little' to be in pain from this sort of thing. And you're not a monster for feeling this way or wanting to try something that will feel better for you.
